3.1.1.1 Recreation
Development of Bad Creek Reservoir would result in a loss of land and water resources now providing limited dispersed outdoor recreation opportunities in the proposed dam and reservoir basin area (see Subsection 2.1.2 herein). In addition, a temporary loss of present limited recreation opportunities would occur within the project borrow and construction areas located outside the impoundment site.
Development of the proposed reservoir would not offer any opportunity for water-based recreation activities because of the public safety hazards associated with fluctuations in water surface levels. Maximum daily drawdown would be 83 reet, while daily refilling would entail a maximum 76-foot increase in surface elevation. As a result, the entire reservoir area would be fenced to prohibit public access.
The proposed 31-mile hiking trail and related features would provide new public recreation opportunities such as hiking, primitive camping, nature study, and related low-density specialized outdoor pursuits for an estimated 1,500 visitors annually. The proposed trail would comprise the central segment of a regional trail system now partially completed, and should be fully compatible with the adjacent limited or primitive-type recreational opportunities emphasized at both Lake Jocassee to the south and the Whitewater River Unit of the Nantahala National Forest to the north.
Construction of the proposed trail developments should have a minimal environmental impact on land features and uses because of the Applicant's stated intention to maintain these areas in the most natural condition possible with very limited facilities development. The 2-foot-wide trail tread would consist of naturally occurring surface materials. Although the exact route of the trail has not been determined, all of it would be outside the project boundary. Approximately one-third of the trail route would incorporate existing trails and primitive roads. Trail segments in two areas would extend some 3 miles through the Whitewater River Unit of the Nantahala National Forest. Close coordination with the Forest Service would be required for continuity in the trail route. Although no recreation facilities now exist in the Unit, the Forest Service intends to construct the North Carolina portion of the Foothills Trail within its jurisdiction and to develop two overlooks, parking, sanitary, and picnic facilities in the upper Whitewater Falls area (Forest Service, NDa and 1974b).
